Retained sleeve order can control the sign of equilibrium binding cooperativity in a single, explicit contact model. The strongest construction now has exactly matched single-site affinities in its aligned-guide limit, yet one retained order makes the second connection less favorable and another makes it more favorable. Small positive guide and docking clearances preserve the opposite signs, although exact matching of the single-site affinities is then only a limiting result.

The resulting operation is a persistent choice of how exchangeable contacts cooperate. Removing the external guests leaves that choice stored in the sleeve order; restoring the guest reservoir restores the corresponding binding law. This is a local constitutive result. A branching material, a mechanism for rewriting the order, and useful molecular exchange rates remain separate requirements.

3. The dock now supplies its own registration and release path

A favorable protrusion position would be insufficient if an ordinary chemical contact allowed the guest to attach in other orientations. I therefore replaced the freely swiveling contact with an explicit key and socket.

The active collar carries an outward-pointing rectangular key, displaced sideways from the intrusive sphere’s path. The guest carries a complementary socket. The only attractive patch is buried on the socket’s closed inner bottom; its partner is on the key tip. The socket walls are thicker than the attraction’s capture range.

This closes two earlier loopholes:

An exposed shoulder patch could have stabilized attachment without full registration.
An incorrectly oriented key or connector could have obstructed removal, even when the final bound pose was collision-free.

In the corrected construction, the guest withdraws radially outward. That motion removes the socket from the key and moves the intrusive sphere away from the collars, relaxing its exclusion. The connector is routed below the root flange before reaching the socket. The revised fixture geometry was checked with segment–box and segment–segment collision tests.

The registration argument is also explicit. In the zero-clearance limit, contact between patches in the interiors of the opposing flat end faces fixes their axial orientation. A

6. What the primary evidence supports, and what remains molecularly missing

The broad mechanisms have strong precedents. Wang and colleagues’ SteriDyn devices already demonstrate steric communication between independently fluctuating DNA-origami arms, including regulation of another arm’s latching. Thus sterically mediated allostery is established experimentally. 
researchgate.net
 Pinson, Sevick and Williams already showed theoretically that the placement and translational entropy of mobile rings can strongly alter a polyrotaxane’s mechanical response. 
The Australian National University

The narrower contribution here is the explicit compatibility of retained order, genuine sliding, removable registered guests and opposite contact cooperativity, with the statistical weights derived from the same contact construction.

DNA provides relevant ingredients. Benson and colleagues demonstrated capped DNA-origami sliders, docking through two or four linker duplexes, and strand-displacement release back to a freely moving state. Their nanometre-scale positioning-fluctuation estimates came from oxDNA simulations; they do not establish the pose distribution of the external socket proposed here. 
Wiley Online Library
 Gerling and colleagues demonstrated shape-complementary DNA interfaces and reversible assembly, but also reported a directly relevant tradeoff: stronger hybridization contacts made opening require conditions that compromised structural integrity, while fewer contacts restored reversibility at the cost of a less well-defined closed state.

That estimate exposes a real cost: tight registration can make capture rare and require substantial binding stabilization. It supplies neither a measured chemical affinity nor a dissociation time. Moreover, a strand-displacement mechanism demonstrated on an accessible slider linkage cannot automatically be transferred to a patch buried at the bottom of a close-fitting socket; access for the release strand would itself require a compatible construction.

The completed advance is therefore a common-contact equilibrium operation with a finite physical regime, together with a constitutive rule and a scaling limit. The remaining molecular task is to realize its registered bound-pose distribution, retention lifetime and exchange kinetics together. The model now states what that realization must accomplish without borrowing an actuator or a favorable ensemble from a separate idealization.

A favorable protrusion position would be insufficient if an ordinary chemical contact allowed the guest to attach in other orientations. I therefore replaced the freely swiveling contact with an explicit key and socket.

The active collar carries an outward-pointing rectangular key, displaced sideways from the intrusive sphere’s path. The guest carries a complementary socket. The only attractive patch is buried on the socket’s closed inner bottom; its partner is on the key tip. The socket walls are thicker than the attraction’s capture range.

This closes two earlier loopholes:

  • An exposed shoulder patch could have stabilized attachment without full registration.
  • An incorrectly oriented key or connector could have obstructed removal, even when the final bound pose was collision-free.

In the corrected construction, the guest withdraws radially outward. That motion removes the socket from the key and moves the intrusive sphere away from the collars, relaxing its exclusion. The connector is routed below the root flange before reaching the socket. The revised fixture geometry was checked with segment–box and segment–segment collision tests.

The registration argument is also explicit. In the zero-clearance limit, contact between patches in the interiors of the opposing flat end faces fixes their axial orientation. A 16×4 nm16\times4\ \mathrm{nm}16×4 nm rectangular key then fits the matching socket only in centered alignment, apart from a possible 180∘180^\circ180∘ roll. An off-center patch removes that remaining ambiguity. The right-hand assembly is a proper rotation of the left-hand one, so it uses the same guest chemistry rather than requiring a mirror-image molecule.

5. The decisive failures still constrain the opportunity

The attempted route from anti-dimer geometry to a branching material failed a stronger test. A spacing design can prevent two rails from using several bonds on each other, yet still admit a finite, fully saturated assembly. I constructed a six-rail K3,3K_{3,3}K3,3​ arrangement—three rails of each kind, all nine cross-connections occupied—with strict clearance margins. It has a finite neighborhood of allowed configurations, so it is not merely an isolated geometric coincidence.

That defeats the claim that suppressing repeated pair bonds necessarily selects an extended network. It does not establish that the finite cage dominates equilibrium.

The original freely swiveling contact also exposed a different failure. Fixed configurations could show strong spectator-mediated coupling of either sign, but integrating over mobile three-dimensional configurations diluted the effect. In the tested ensemble, only about 0.03%0.03\%0.03% of proposed geometries let both neighbors restrict the same spectator; the resulting joint-weight suppression was approximately 0.036%0.036\%0.036%. The registered guest addresses that specific lack of contact.

The one-contact washout and ordinary-binder comparison remain intact. In particular, an ordinary receptor with the same full internal steric ensemble can reproduce the present response. What the construction adds is a physical way for a nonpassing, mobile internal sequence to determine that ensemble and retain it through external bond loss.

6. What the primary evidence supports, and what remains molecularly missing

The broad mechanisms have strong precedents. Wang and colleagues’ SteriDyn devices already demonstrate steric communication between independently fluctuating DNA-origami arms, including regulation of another arm’s latching. Thus sterically mediated allostery is established experimentally. researchgate.net Pinson, Sevick and Williams already showed theoretically that the placement and translational entropy of mobile rings can strongly alter a polyrotaxane’s mechanical response. The Australian National University

The narrower contribution here is the explicit compatibility of retained order, genuine sliding, removable registered guests and opposite contact cooperativity, with the statistical weights derived from the same contact construction.

DNA provides relevant ingredients. Benson and colleagues demonstrated capped DNA-origami sliders, docking through two or four linker duplexes, and strand-displacement release back to a freely moving state. Their nanometre-scale positioning-fluctuation estimates came from oxDNA simulations; they do not establish the pose distribution of the external socket proposed here. Wiley Online Library Gerling and colleagues demonstrated shape-complementary DNA interfaces and reversible assembly, but also reported a directly relevant tradeoff: stronger hybridization contacts made opening require conditions that compromised structural integrity, while fewer contacts restored reversibility at the cost of a less well-defined closed state. researchgate.net

The finite socket calculation makes that tradeoff concrete. With 0.25 nm0.25\ \mathrm{nm}0.25 nm transverse clearance and a 0.5 nm0.5\ \mathrm{nm}0.5 nm capture radius, a restricted orientation integral gave a capture factor of approximately

1.3×10−8 nm3,1.3\times10^{-8}\ \mathrm{nm^3},1.3×10−8 nm3,

using rotations normalized to unit measure. This is a contribution from a checked pose region, not a completed integral over every possible binding orientation. Under a square-well association approximation, if that region alone supplied binding, a 1 μM1\ \mu\mathrm M1 μM guest reservoir would require roughly 34 kBT34\,k_BT34kB​T of stabilization to reach the illustrated occupancy regime.

That estimate exposes a real cost: tight registration can make capture rare and require substantial binding stabilization. It supplies neither a measured chemical affinity nor a dissociation time. Moreover, a strand-displacement mechanism demonstrated on an accessible slider linkage cannot automatically be transferred to a patch buried at the bottom of a close-fitting socket; access for the release strand would itself require a compatible construction.

The completed advance is therefore a common-contact equilibrium operation with a finite physical regime, together with a constitutive rule and a scaling limit. The remaining molecular task is to realize its registered bound-pose distribution, retention lifetime and exchange kinetics together. The model now states what that realization must accomplish without borrowing an actuator or a favorable ensemble from a separate idealization.
